title: The full moon
hookLine: Buddhist observance days fall on the full moon; King Bimbisara asks the Buddha to gather his monks on the moon's days
tomorrow: Jesus took his friends away to rest. who was waiting on the shore?

lines: FULL MOON NIGHTS PULL PEOPLE OUT.
cards: Full moon nights have a way of pulling people outside. King Bimbisara noticed something like that in his own kingdom.

Wandering teachers of other groups gathered on the moon's days, and people came to hear them and grew fond of them. So the king went to the Buddha with a request: could the Buddha's monks gather on those days too?

teach.b: The Buddha agreed. But the first time the monks gathered, they simply sat there in silence, and the people who came were annoyed: why sit like that and say nothing?
So the Buddha told the monks that on these days they should speak the teaching. Later he added the recitation of the monks' rules. That's the root of uposatha, the observance day.

It still follows the moon: the full moon, the new moon and the quarter moons between. Monks recite their rules together, and lay Buddhists visit the temple, listen to teaching, and some keep extra precepts for the day.
Under it is a teaching: the moon gives a community a regular time to come back, renew its promises and hear the teaching again. This week ran the same way. Longer silence, past the wind and the fire.
The week, with day two still waiting for its good. Screen-free, a fenced rest. Play, David before the ark.
My week, Benedict's page. The new moon, looked for together.
The full moon is a good night to walk them all back through.

how: In Theravada countries, uposatha days fall on the full moon, the new moon and the quarter moons; monks recite the Patimokkha, and lay Buddhists may visit the temple, hear a talk and keep the eight precepts for the day.

practice: Stand and walk slowly across the room and back, one step for each line of the week: longer silence, the week, screen-free, play, my week, the new moon.
Then find the date of the next full moon and choose a route for a walk under it.

wordCard.voice: The full moon: an uposatha night, when a Buddhist community gathers to hear the teaching and renew its promises.

orig.note: Pali: the observance day, kept at the moon's turning points.

carryVoice: Your line: the full moon. The monks sat silent until the Buddha said: speak the teaching. Good night.
